AUTHOR: Petrellis
TITLE: Fish Monitoring from Low-Contrast Underwater Images
SPECIES: Mediterranean seabreams (Diplodus sargus/annularis, Oblada melanura, Pagrus pagrus, etc.)
DATA: Own UVIMEF dataset (60 videos, 720 photos; low-cost TurboX camera, shallow coastal waters)
V_EV: Sec. 3.1: 'captured both during sunny and cloudy days with calm or stormy seas at a depth between 0.5 and 3 m.'
D2: 270 train / 52 test fish patches (from 400 frames of 60 videos)
D_EV: Sec. 3.1: '400 image frames have been used to generate 322 single fish image patches... training... using 270 of these image patches and the rest... for testing.'
R_EV: Sec. 3.3: pre-trained detector from [4] 'proved extremely sensitive for our dataset and even fish that were hardly recognized with the naked eye have been detected' - qualitative only.
C_EV: no statement found (Table 8 text: COD direction used 'only if the confidence is above a threshold' - value not reported)
E_EV: Table 7: 'Error and standard deviation in measuring relative fish length and height' - Fish length error 5.4%, height error 4.5%, vs landmarks annotated on same images.
ARCH: Pre-trained TensorFlow fish detector (Faster R-CNN based, repo [4]) + Ensemble of Regression Trees (ERT/DEST) 18-landmark shape alignment + PCA/template-matching orientation + centroid tracking; FPGA acceleration
METR: landmark relative/absolute error, relative length/height error, orientation success rate, latency
NOTE: Platform not stated (low-cost action camera, 'camera that was not stable'; possibly handheld/snorkel) -> PLAT NR. Length is RELATIVE (pixel) length/height; ground truth = landmarks annotated in LAE editor on same images. R1=Y only via off-the-shelf pre-trained detector applied qualitatively to own data (training domain of [4] unknown); main ERT models trained/tested on own data only. Dataset UVIMEF public on Kaggle [34].
AUTHORS_FULL: Petrellis, N; Keramidas, G; Antonopoulos, CP; Voros, N
